page: Vultr vx1-g-32c-128g-1920s is a general-purpose server belonging to the VX1 Cloud Compute family. It features a dedicated AMD EPYC x86_64 processor with 32 vCPUs, mapped from 16 physical cores with 2 threads per core. The processor operates at a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz and includes 32 MB of L3 cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 48 KB of L1d cache. The system is equipped with 128.0 GB of system memory, yielding a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per core. Local storage is bundled and consists of a 1920 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. No GPU accelerators are present on this configuration.

Benchmark data reveals strong memory and single-core execution capabilities. The server achieves top-tier performance in stress-ng single-core CPU tests, single-threaded gzip compression, and single-threaded bzip3 decompression. Large-block memory write bandwidth and the PassMark memory score also rank in the top tier. Multi-core performance is more moderate, with stress-ng multi-core CPU performance and small-block read-only memory bandwidth falling into the average category. However, PassMark CPU scores, database operations, and Redis SET operations remain strong, placing in the top quarter of tested hardware. For LLM workloads, the server shows top-tier text generation speeds for small and medium models, though prompt processing for larger models scales down to average performance.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the vx1-g-32c-128g-1920s offers a balanced resource density, combining dedicated AMD EPYC compute cores with a substantial 128 GB memory footprint and fast NVMe storage without the premium of specialized GPU hardware. This makes it highly suitable for general-purpose enterprise workloads, relational and NoSQL database hosting, static web serving, and moderate-scale data processing or text-based machine learning inference. The lack of hardware acceleration limits its suitability for heavy deep learning training, but its strong single-core performance and fast local NVMe storage make it an efficient choice for I/O-heavy and database-centric applications.
